short: The first significant victory of the Russian Navy, proving its effectiveness against the Swedish fleet.
full:
Fought on 7 August 1714, the Battle of Gangut took place off the Hanko Peninsula in Finland. A large Russian galley fleet, personally overseen by Peter the Great, engaged and defeated a smaller detachment of the Swedish navy. Utilizing their shallow-draft galleys in the calm coastal waters, the Russians outmaneuvered the heavier Swedish sailing ships.

The Russian boarding actions successfully captured the Swedish vessels. The victory was a major morale boost for Russia and demonstrated the viability of Peter's newly constructed navy. It allowed the Russian fleet to dominate the Gulf of Finland and project power directly against the Swedish coastline.
